messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for customer OrionMed (dedicated pool: orionmed-eu1). p95=480ms, p99=1.9s over last 5m. SLO=250ms. Paging on-call. links: https://metrics.internal/redwood/orionmed-eu1 -> graph
oncall-ryan: @incident-bot acknowledged. paging SRE oncall. I'm on it. starting triage. :mag_right:
sre-anya: I'm in. pulling pool metrics now. initial glance — GPU utilization high (95%), KV cache miss rate up x5, tail latency correlated with seq-length spikes. suspect tenant noise or sudden traffic pattern change.
eng-runtime-lead: FYI could be KV cache churn + long-context requests. if KV gets evicted we see p99 spikes. consider tenant isolation + fall back to quantized variant if we need immediate relief.
oncall-ryan: running quick checks:
```
# check top tenants by qps
rwdctl pools tail orionmed-eu1 --metrics top-tenants --window 5m
```
output shows tenant_id=orion_ops (38% qps), tenant_id=research_lab (22%), many long-seq requests from research_lab.
sre-anya: research_lab is spiking with seq lengths ~8k tokens. that's hammering memory and KV. propose isolating research_lab to its own constrained pool or throttling their max tokens temporarily. pinging @account-manager-liz to confirm customer impact.
account-manager-liz: confirming — research_lab is an internal team at OrionMed running batch transcripts. they do not expect real-time latency for interactive users. we can ask them to shift batch jobs to off-peak or accept throttling for now. I'll open a ticket on their side and message their ops.
eng-runtime-lead: recommend immediate mitigations in order:
1) throttle research_lab token length to 1024 for 10m
2) isolate research_lab to tenant_isolate slot (preserve dedicated capacity for interactive customers)
3) spin up warm spare pool and route 20% of interactive traffic there
4) if needed, fallback interactive route to quantized model variant v2-q4 to reduce latency/cost
we can do 1-2 quickly.
oncall-ryan: starting throttle + isolate now:
```
# throttle tokens
rwdctl tenants throttle research_lab --max-tokens 1024 --duration 10m
# tenant isolation
rwdctl tenants isolate research_lab --pool orionmed-eu1-isolated-1
```
infra-bot: ACTION: Tenant throttle request received. Applying policy. ETA ~30s.
infra-bot: ACTION: Tenant isolation started. provisioning isolated slot orionmed-eu1-isolated-1 (GPU x2). ETA ~2m.
sre-anya: KV cache miss rate dropping after throttle, p95 now 310ms, p99 820ms and trending down. still above SLO but improving. keep isolation + monitor.
eng-runtime-lead: while provisioning completes, let's route a small percentage of interactive traffic to warm spare to reduce queuing. command:
```
rwdctl route update --pool orionmed-eu1 --add-target orionmed-eu1-warmspare --weight 20
```
oncall-ryan: applied route change. infra-bot confirms traffic shift.
infra-bot: ROUTE UPDATE: 20% traffic to orionmed-eu1-warmspare active.
sre-anya: live numbers now: p95 200-260ms, p99 ~420ms. -> SLO window for p95 mostly green, p99 still borderline during spikes. good improvement. monitor for 15m.
account-manager-liz: messaging OrionMed ops: "We've isolated your batch tenant and throttled long-context requests to protect interactive users. Expect degraded throughput for research_lab for ~30min while we stabilize. Will send follow-up." :memo:
customer-ops-jason: OrionMed ops acknowledged. They ask whether we can provision a longer-term isolated pool for research_lab outside business hours — will coordinate after incident.
eng-runtime-lead: next steps if p99 resurges: fallback interactive route to v2-q4 (quantized model) for 100% of new sessions for 10m while we do deeper root cause. Command:
```
rwdctl model route --pool orionmed-eu1 --model v2-q4 --session-filter interactive --duration 10m
```
oncall-ryan: keeping logs and saving graphs. creating incident Jira: RWD-INC-12458 and linking OrionMed ticket.
sre-anya: can someone check autoscaler events? maybe scale was inhibited by placement constraints.
infra-bot: AUTOSCALER LOGS -> recent: attempted scale +2 nodes @1758889800 failed due to zone capacity in eu-west-1c. Fallback to pending queue. Suggest manual scale to other zone.
eng-runtime-lead: ok let's manually add nodes in eu-west-1b to relieve. running:
```
rwdctl pools scale orionmed-eu1 --add 2 --zone eu-west-1b
```
infra-bot: SCALE: provisioning 2 nodes in eu-west-1b. ETA ~4m. will report when healthy.
sre-anya: thanks. after scale completes we'll re-evaluate KV eviction policy and adjust cache sizes for high seq workloads.
oncall-ryan: update after infra: p95=170ms, p99=290ms. autoscaler back to normal and no further pages in last 8m. marking incident as contained but keeping channel open for 30m for observation. :white_check_mark:
account-manager-liz: passing incident summary to customer: brief impact, mitigations (throttled batch tenant, isolated tenant, scaled pool, route adjustments), next steps (follow-up about dedicated scheduled isolate or quota). customer thanks the team.
eng-runtime-lead: postmortem items:
- root cause: unthrottled long-context batch jobs leading to KV cache churn + zone capacity limiting autoscaler
- action: add soft limit on token length per tenant by default, improve autoscaler zone fallback, add alert rule for long-seq-runaway
- owner: eng-runtime
oncall-ryan: assigning follow-ups in Jira and will create a short runbook PR for tenant long-context policies.
sre-anya: leaving handoff to eng-runtime for deeper root cause and to account-manager for customer coordination. I'll update status page if anything changes. thanks all. :bow:
incident-bot: UPDATE: incident classified as "contained". no active SLO breaches for last 10m. Incident lead: oncall-ryan. Postmortem required. link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/1758889990
oncall-ryan: ending channel monitoring but keeping it readable for 30m. anyone else? otherwise closing thread.
customer-ops-jason: thanks team — appreciate the quick isolation. will follow up with scheduling for long-run isolated capacity.
eng-runtime-lead: noted. will own follow-up tasks. closing in 30.
